title: Describe actions, states, people, and purposes

grammarPoints.title: Describe an activity in progress
grammarPoints.meaning: Use ている for an activity that is continuing at the time you are discussing. It can also describe an ongoing habit or occupation when the context makes that meaning clear.
grammarPoints.formation: Activity verb te-form + います / いません / いました / いませんでした.
notes: Choose a durative activity such as reading, eating, or drinking for an “is doing” interpretation.
ある and いる already express states and do not take another ている here. Change verbs have a different interpretation, introduced next.
The helper いる always conjugates as a る-verb. Its use is not limited to living subjects.

examples.japanese: 秋さんは新聞を読んでいます。
examples.kana: あきさんはしんぶんをよんでいます。

examples.japanese: 蓮さんは水を飲んでいました。
examples.kana: れんさんはみずをのんでいました。

schemas.context: Describe what you can see right now. Use polite speech.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: Only durative activity verbs are admitted for the ongoing meaning.

Inflect the auxiliary いる, not the verb’s te-form.

schemas.context: Describe this person’s continuing occupation, not what they are doing at this moment. Use polite speech.
schemas.kana: {person}はにほんごをおしえています。
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: The occupation context gives ている an ongoing professional meaning.

grammarPoints.title: Describe a state resulting from a change
grammarPoints.meaning: With a change verb, ている often describes the state after the change: someone is married, seated, awake, dressed, or has gone somewhere.
grammarPoints.formation: Change verb te-form + います, with the verb’s usual particles.
notes: 知っています means “knows”; its ordinary negative is 知りません, not 知っていません.
住んでいます describes where someone lives. 持っています commonly means “has”.
行っています / 来ています normally describe someone who has gone or arrived, not someone traveling right now.
着ています means wearing clothing, not necessarily putting it on. Use clothing appropriate to 着る, such as shirts and sweaters.

examples.japanese: 美緒さんは大阪に住んでいます。
examples.kana: みおさんはおおさかにすんでいます。

examples.japanese: 秋さんは蓮さんを知っています。
examples.kana: あきさんはれんさんをしっています。

schemas.context: Describe a current place of residence politely.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: Use に for residence. 住みます alone does not express the same current residential state.

schemas.context: Describe an item this person owns. Use polite speech.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: Select an ownable item; the intended meaning is possession, not an action of picking it up.

schemas.context: Describe what someone is wearing now. Use polite speech.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: 着る accepts upper-body clothing here. Do not insert shoes, glasses, or hats.

schemas.context: Say whether these two people are acquainted. Use polite speech.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: Use distinct people.
The negative of “know” is 知りません in this pattern.

schemas.context: Say whether these two people are acquainted. Use polite speech.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: Use distinct people.
The negative of “know” is 知りません in this pattern.

schemas.context: Explain why the person is away. They have already arrived at their destination. Use polite speech.
schemas.english: {person} has gone to {city} and is still there.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: 行っています has the result-state interpretation. Do not prompt “is on the way to”.
The English explanation makes the state explicit; no extra Japanese clause is needed.

grammarPoints.title: Describe someone’s physical features
grammarPoints.meaning: Introduce a person as the topic and describe one of their features with が.
grammarPoints.formation: Person は body part が adjective です.
notes: Use natural body-part/adjective pairings: 髪が長い, 目が大きい, and so on.
背が高い / 低い mean tall / short; 頭がいい means smart. These are established expressions, not literal possession.
Do not mechanically translate English “has” with 持っています for body features.

examples.japanese: 蓮さんは目が大きいです。
examples.kana: れんさんはめがおおきいです。

schemas.context: Give a neutral physical description politely.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: The adjective must accept the body-part category.
Do not use 持っています for the English “has” here.

schemas.context: Describe someone’s height politely.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: Use the idiom 背が高い or 背が低い, not 長い for a tall person.

grammarPoints.title: Join adjective and noun descriptions
grammarPoints.meaning: Link two descriptions without repeating complete sentences. The final predicate gives the tense.
grammarPoints.formation: い-adjective: final い → くて (いい → よくて). な-adjective base + で. Noun + で. Then the next description.
notes: Do not use と to connect adjective predicates.
Choose compatible qualities for the same subject, and avoid accidentally repeating the same quality.
な is for modifying nouns; use で, not なで, to connect a な-adjective predicate.

examples.english: The watch is new and inexpensive.
examples.japanese: 時計は新しくて、安いです。
examples.kana: とけいはあたらしくて、やすいです。

examples.english: Mio is a student and is kind.
examples.japanese: 美緒さんは学生で、親切です。
examples.kana: みおさんはがくせいで、しんせつです。

schemas.context: Give two compatible descriptions in one polite sentence.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: Use two distinct qualities. The first is in te-form and the second carries politeness.

schemas.context: Recall a place you visited. Use one polite sentence in the past.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: The final predicate carries past tense. Use distinct qualities.

schemas.context: Introduce someone with two facts in polite speech.
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: で links the first noun predicate; it is not a location particle here.

grammarPoints.title: Go somewhere in order to do something
grammarPoints.meaning: State the purpose of movement, such as going to a library to read.
grammarPoints.formation: Destination に / へ + action phrase ending in the verb’s ます stem + に + 行く / 来る / 帰る.
notes: The purpose verb uses its stem, not dictionary form or te-form. Its object retains を.
The destination must be a sensible place for the activity. 来る moves toward the speaker; 帰る returns to a home or usual base.
Some activity nouns can fill the purpose position, such as 買い物に行く. 遊びに行く means going to have fun or visit, not playing an instrument or sport.

examples.english: I went to the library to read a newspaper.
examples.japanese: 図書館に新聞を読みに行きました。
examples.kana: としょかんにしんぶんをよみにいきました。

schemas.context: Explain the purpose of an earlier trip politely.
schemas.omission: The speaker is understood.
restrictions: The destination permits reading.
Use 読み, the stem, before purpose に; keep the motion verb past.

schemas.context: Explain a future plan politely.
schemas.english: I will go to {place} to eat {food}.
schemas.omission: The speaker is understood.
restrictions: The destination permits a meal. 食べ is the stem of 食べる.

schemas.context: You are away from home and will return there for a drink. Use polite speech.
schemas.english: I will go back home to drink {drink}.
schemas.japanese: 家に{drink}を飲みに帰ります。
schemas.kana: いえに{drink}をのみにかえります。
schemas.omission: The speaker is understood.
restrictions: 帰る requires returning to a usual base, which is home in this schema.

grammarPoints.title: Count people
grammarPoints.meaning: Use the counter 人 for people and combine it with います to say how many are present.
grammarPoints.formation: Place に(は) + person noun が + number of people + います.
notes: 一人 is ひとり, 二人 is ふたり, and 四人 is よにん. Ask 何人（なんにん）.
The counter follows が without a further particle. 人 does not count animals or things.
A location can be introduced with には when it is the topic or contrasts with another location.

examples.english: There are four teachers in the library.
examples.japanese: 図書館に先生が四人います。
examples.kana: としょかんにせんせいがよにんいます。

schemas.context: Report how many people are present using polite speech.
schemas.omission: Keep the location to distinguish this group from people elsewhere.
restrictions: Use human nouns and the 人 counter.
This plural English template uses quantities of two or more.

schemas.context: Report a single person’s presence politely.
schemas.kana: この{place}に{person}がひとりいます。
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: 一人 has the irregular reading ひとり.

schemas.context: Ask politely for the number of people.
schemas.japanese: この{place}に{people}が何人いますか。
schemas.kana: この{place}に{people}がなんにんいますか。
schemas.omission: The topic may be omitted when clear from context; the model states it when shown.
restrictions: Use 何人（なんにん）, not 何枚.
